lines.text: The male drops in from above, and the gooseneck seats. This time we mark it out and cut it, step by step, following one training course.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: That course's exercise adds a short stub tenon under the seat. We'll leave it out and follow the steps for the joint itself.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: First, mark which piece is which. The male is the upper piece; on a sill, the anchor bolt goes in it, beside the splice.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Center lines go on both pieces first, as in episode one. The neck and head are laid out from them.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: On the female, the course marks the end line first. Then the seat lines, the lines for the neck and the head's tip, and the cut line.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: The neck lines are split evenly from the center line, using the width of the sashigane's blade, about fifteen millimeters, each side.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress. Say 'sashi-gah-neh' as sa-shi-ga-ne, four short even syllables.
lines.tts: The neck lines are split evenly from the center line, using the width of the sashi-gah-neh's blade, about fifteen millimeters, each side.

lines.text: The head's slanted lines also use the blade's width, running from the tip toward the neck. Then the seat lines are carried down both side faces.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: The male gets the same lines, in the same order: the end line, the neck and tip lines and the cut line, the neck lines from the center, the slanted head lines, and the seat lines down both sides.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Cutting the female. Rip down the end grain, leaving half the line, and angle the saw so it doesn't cut into the seat. Then crosscut to free the seat.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Chop the head's tip straight down first, then its sides, then clear out the socket.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: The course digs a little past the line at the tip, about three millimeters, and checks that the floor is flat and level with the seat.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Where the head meets the neck, it also digs about three millimeters past the line, toward the tip, to allow for a slight slope on the head's bearing faces.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Cutting the male. Rip down to the seat and crosscut the shoulder, leaving half the line.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Rip the head's sides down to the neck, leaving the line at the top and taking it at the bottom, so it enters easily and tightens as it seats.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Crosscut short of the neck line and split the waste off. Saw the bearing slope with kerfs about a chisel's width apart, and chop the neck to its line, with the same taper.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Finally, pare the slope smooth, and chamfer the bearing edges of the head and neck.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Then the male drops in from above, onto the seat.
lines.instr: A calm, warm, unhurried documentary narrator teaching a hand craft to a friend. Slow, steady pace of about 125 words per minute, with a short natural pause after each sentence. Japanese words are pronounced the Japanese way: even syllables, short crisp vowels, no English stress.

lines.text: Center lines first. Mark both pieces the same way, split the neck from the center, and cut so the head enters easily and tightens.
